fields.description:
Forward-looking, LOW. Not a failure on main today.

## What is actually true

tests/unit/test_advanced_cli_parsers.py::test_audit_cli_unknown_subcommand_exits_2_through_the_factory asserts that argparse error output starts with "usage:". On Python 3.14 argparse colorizes help and error output BY DEFAULT, so the captured stderr begins with an ANSI escape:

    "\x1b[1;34musage: \x1b[0m\x1b[1;35mrebar audit\x1b[0m ..."

and startswith("usage:") is False.

## Evidence, both directions

- FAILS on Python 3.14.7: 1 failed.
- PASSES on Python 3.12.13: 1 passed. .github/python-version.txt pins 3.12, and CI runs 3.11/3.12/3.13, so CI is green and main is NOT broken.
- NO_COLOR=1 makes it pass on 3.14, confirming color is the whole cause.

## How this surfaced, and the correction

It was first reported to me as "a pre-existing failure on main". That framing was wrong, and the cause was mine: I briefed a subagent to provision a worktree with a bare , which inherits the host ambient interpreter (3.14.7 here) instead of the pinned one. AGENTS.md warns about exactly this — use → uv venv --python 3.12 .venv   (pinned by .github/python-version.txt)

ERROR: could not provision .venv on Python 3.12.
       That version is what CI tests (.github/python-version.txt); this host's
       ambient python3 is Python 3.14.7.
       Refusing to fall back to it — a venv on an untested interpreter yields
       local failures CI cannot reproduce, and masks the ones that matter.
       Let uv fetch the right one:  uv python install 3.12 / usage: make worktree name=<branch> [dir=<path>]
  Creates a worktree at <path> (default ../<branch>) branched from a freshly-
  fetched origin/main, then provisions .venv + editable install + the pre-commit gate., and treat an ambient-toolchain failure as an environment error rather than repository evidence. Filing the accurate finding rather than the alarming one.

## Why it is still worth fixing

The project will hit this the moment it adds 3.14 to the CI matrix, and it is a brittle-assertion class we have already been bitten by in this epic: asserting on RENDERED text rather than on behaviour.

## Approach

Make the assertion color-independent. Either strip ANSI before asserting, or force plain output for the test (argparse accepts color=False on 3.14; NO_COLOR is the portable env-level lever). Prefer whichever keeps the test asserting the OBSERVABLE contract — exit code 2 and a usage line — without depending on terminal styling. Audit sibling tests in the same file for the same pattern.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC1: the test passes on both Python 3.12 and Python 3.14. Verified by running it under both interpreters.
- [x] AC2: it still fails if the CLI stops emitting a usage line or stops exiting 2. Verified by mutation.
- [x] AC3: sibling assertions in the file that match on rendered argparse text are audited and given the same treatment, or explicitly noted as safe.

## Testing

- python -m pytest tests/unit/test_advanced_cli_parsers.py -q under 3.12 and 3.14 — AC1-AC3.
- make lint && make typecheck.

## Completion evidence (2026-09-03) — Gerrit change 2568 MERGED

- **AC1** — verified on BOTH interpreters. 3.12.13 (what CI pins and runs): 713 passed, 1 skipped. 3.14.7 (a throwaway venv built for this): was 25 failures, now 624 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed.
- **AC2** — verified by mutation, two ways, against `render_parse_error` in `_cli/_parser.py`, which is the path this test actually exercises. Mutant A (`return 2` -> `return 0`): FAILED, `assert 0 == 2`. Mutant B (suppress the usage write): FAILED, `assert False`. Restored: passes. So the assertion binds on the exit code AND on the usage line, not merely on one of them.
- **AC3** — the audit went well beyond this file. Running the 31 test modules that assert on argparse help/usage text under 3.14 found **25 failures across 9 modules**, all now fixed by the same one-line change. Two of them were PRODUCT regressions rather than brittle assertions: `gen_cli_help.py --check` reported every committed `help/*.txt` stale, and `RebarHelpFormatter._format_usage` wraps on rendered line length, which ANSI escapes inflate — so usage would wrap differently for real users.

Fix: `RebarArgumentParser.__init__` sets `self.color = False`. In 3.14 `ArgumentParser._get_formatter` calls `formatter._set_color(self.color)`, so that attribute is the entire knob; subparsers inherit it via `parser_class`. The attribute does not exist before 3.14, where the assignment is inert. No new mechanism (ratchet reports new=0) — a `NO_COLOR` autouse fixture was rejected for that reason and because it would have masked the two product regressions rather than fixing them.

Trigger worth recording: this needs Python 3.14 AND `_colorize.can_colorize()` true, which requires a TTY or `FORCE_COLOR` in the environment. Plain CI with neither would have stayed green even after moving to 3.14, so the defect would have reached users before it reached the build.

Deliberate follow-up, NOT fixed here: `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:147` builds `bridge suggest-mapping`'s parser as a bare `argparse.ArgumentParser`, outside the RebarArgumentParser family, so its help still colorizes on 3.14 — and it also misses every other RebarArgumentParser behaviour. No test covers it; pulling it onto the shared factory is wider than this ticket.
